data.ruling: The refutation stands. The rule for "function requirements: FUNCTION" (tools/research/round1.js:266, tools/research/README.md:258-260) says the function's requirement list must name every requirement that IOBoard.md, the answers, and the values found for research under "Raised by P1" set for that function, and no value in the list may be weaker than theirs. IOBoard.md sets "520 kB SRAM on the die" for the Microcontroller in both the Summary row (:53) and the Microcontroller requirement row (:103). Research.md:47 states the same figure as a fixed input. The claim's list takes 48 GPIO, 8 ADC inputs and "no PSRAM" from that same line but has no SRAM entry. So the list does not name every requirement IOBoard.md sets for the function, and this omission is enough for the refutation to stand. Two further omissions support it. IOBoard.md:105 relies on a pad input leakage of 1 uA maximum with no IOVDD condition, and the R1 row asks R1 to confirm the Table 1433 figures, the input leakage among them. IOBoard.md:123 fixes QSPI_SS at QFN-80 pin 75 and RUN at pin 35 for BOOT and RESET; this is also missing, though it is a pin assignment rather than a qualifying value. The datasheet meets the SRAM value: build 2025-07-29 gives "520 kB on-chip SRAM". The fault is in the list, not the part. The scope is function: the finding concerns what this function's list must carry, not the RP2354B's lifecycle, end-of-life notice, maker allowlist or LCSC identity. The V1, V2, V4 and V7 entries were not found weaker than their answers, and nothing in this ruling depends on them.
data.evidence: IOBoard.md:53 (Summary, Microcontroller): "RP2354B: ... 48 GPIO ..., 8 ADC ... inputs, 520 kB SRAM (static random-access memory) | decided". IOBoard.md:103 (Microcontroller): "48 GPIO, 8 ADC inputs, 520 kB SRAM on the die, no PSRAM ... in the package ... | decided". Research.md:47 (fixed inputs): "48 GPIO ..., 8 ADC inputs, 520 kB SRAM ... on the die, no PSRAM". The claim's 15 entries (part, stepping, package, GPIO count, ADC inputs, in-package flash, flash supply range, GPIO0-39 fault tolerance, GPIO40-47 rating, pad pull-up, SWDIO reset bias, USB device port, operating ambient, watchdog window, image watchdog timeout) contain no SRAM entry. IOBoard.md:105: "It gives a pin input leakage of 1 µA at most, with no condition on IOVDD; 1 µA drops 2.2 mV across 2.2 kΩ". This input-leakage figure is also not in the claim. Research.md:279 (R1 row): "The pad pull-up of 32 to 86 kΩ and the input leakage are in Table 1433 (Digital IO)", which R1 confirms. IOBoard.md:123: "BOOT pulls QSPI_SS (QFN-80 pin 75 ...) ... RESET pulls RUN (pin 35 ...)". The RP2350 datasheet text copy (build-date 2025-07-29, line 790) reads "520 kB on-chip SRAM, in 10 independent banks" and at line 101199 "Pin Input Leakage IIN 1 μA". The part meets both values; the list omits them. The rule text is tools/research/round1.js:266: "whether the function's requirement list names every requirement set for it by IOBoard.md, the answers and each value found for research ... with no value weaker than theirs".
